source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Flexential Minneapolis - Chaska publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, the only megawatt figure disclosed by any of Minnesota's 13 mapped data center operators, making it the state's largest by reported spec.

The facility spans 160,838 square feet of technical space. That footprint could accommodate roughly 225 racks at 40 kW per rack, a density used in AI training, or roughly 900 racks at 10 kW per rack, a density used in colocation. The operator does not disclose how the power and space are actually allocated, so the facility's actual composition remains unknown from published data.

The certifications indicate regulatory qualifications rather than use. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to control auditing. PCI DSS qualifies the facility for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for export-controlled defense and aerospace work. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security frameworks. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. These certifications do not reveal which tenants occupy the space or what workloads run there.

Minnesota's data center ecosystem remains largely unquantified. Twelve other facilities this site has mapped publish no megawatt figures, so their true power availability is unknown from operator spec pages. The state's actual data center capacity could exceed the 9 MW reported here by an order of magnitude or more.
